mechanisms.name: Primary cilia assembly: IFT machinery, distal appendages, CPLANE module, and transition zone organization
mechanisms.summary: Multiple program genes encode established ciliopathy proteins required for building primary cilia in mammalian cells. Cep164, a distal appendage protein, recruits TTBK2 to basal bodies to initiate ciliogenesis. Wdpcp (a CPLANE protein) recruits IFT-A particles to basal bodies for intraflagellar transport. Cc2d2a localizes to the transition zone and controls protein entry into cilia via Rab8-dependent vesicle trafficking. Nme7 (NME7) is a γ-tubulin ring complex component that maintains primary cilium assembly and ciliary microtubule stability. Ift74 is an IFT-B subunit essential for ciliary assembly through tubulin transport. Tbc1d32 is required for ciliogenesis and downstream Hedgehog signaling. Sdccag8 is a centrosomal ciliopathy protein whose loss causes nephronophthisis-related ciliopathy. Together these genes define a cilia biogenesis gene network active in mouse brain endothelial cells during postnatal development.

mechanisms.name: BBSome-mediated ciliary GPCR trafficking and Hedgehog pathway regulation
mechanisms.summary: Bbs9 encodes a core subunit of the BBSome, an octameric complex that associates with the IFT-B complex to mediate retrograde trafficking of ciliary G protein-coupled receptors including Smoothened (Smo) and GPR161. Loss of Bbs9/BBSome disrupts export of these Hedgehog pathway GPCRs, impairing Hedgehog signal transduction. Nme7 (NME7) maintains Smo localization within primary cilia, with NME7 knockout causing reduced Smo in cilia and impaired Hedgehog signaling; Nme7 knockout in rats and mice produces primary ciliary dyskinesia (hydrocephalus, situs inversus). Tbc1d32 mutant mice show Sonic hedgehog signaling failure as the primary cause of cochlear ciliopathy. Together these genes represent the functional signaling output of the primary cilia — Hedgehog pathway transduction via proper ciliary GPCR trafficking and localization.

mechanisms.name: Mitochondrial inner membrane organization and protein biogenesis
mechanisms.summary: A secondary gene cluster represents mitochondrial function. Chchd6 encodes a core component of the MICOS (Mitochondrial Contact Site and Cristae Organizing System) complex that physically interacts with Mitofilin and Sam50 to sustain inner mitochondrial membrane cristae structure; Chchd6 knockout alters mitochondrial morphology in mice and cells. Metap1d encodes the mitochondrial isoform of methionine aminopeptidase type 1D, which cleaves the N-terminal initiator methionine from nascent mitochondrial proteins — a critical protein maturation step in the mitochondrial matrix. Together these genes suggest a secondary role in mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane organization in brain endothelial cells, potentially supporting the high metabolic demands of barrier-forming endothelia during postnatal brain development.

mechanisms.name: Mitochondrial metabolic function: BCAA catabolism, cristae integrity, and co-factor metabolism
mechanisms.summary: A secondary cluster of genes encodes mitochondrial metabolic functions: Bckdhb encodes the E1-beta subunit of the branched-chain keto acid dehydrogenase complex (BCKD), whose loss causes maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) and cardiac BCAA accumulation; Clybl is a mitochondrial citramalyl-CoA lyase required for itaconate/B12 metabolism; Chchd6 (CHCM1) is a mitochondrial inner membrane protein essential for cristae morphology and oxidative phosphorylation; Metap1d is the mitochondrial methionine aminopeptidase isoform 1D that processes nascent mitochondrial proteins. Together these suggest that maintenance of mitochondrial metabolic homeostasis is a feature of this endothelial cell program, consistent with the high metabolic demands of brain endothelial cells maintaining BBB integrity.

mechanisms.name: Angiogenic tip cell sprouting and vascular network formation in brain endothelium
mechanisms.summary: Angpt2, Cxcr4, Tnfrsf11b, and Cdc42ep3 converge on endothelial tip cell behavior and angiogenic sprouting during postnatal brain vascularization. Angpt2 destabilizes vessels by antagonizing the Tek/Tie2 receptor to promote angiogenic sprouting, and its expression marks the tip cell transcriptome in pericyte-deficient brain ECs. Cxcr4 chemokine signaling controls arterial-venous network formation in the developing brain, expressed in unperfused capillaries with tip-cell-like identity and downregulated upon arterial connection. The regulator Nrp1 promotes tip cell function in brain angiogenesis via CDC42 activation—directly engaging the Cdc42ep3/Borg effector pathway for filopodia formation. Tnfrsf11b/OPG supports endothelial cell survival and angiogenic cord formation. Tek (log2fc +0.39 on knockout) normally opposes this angiogenic program, consistent with Angpt2 antagonizing Tek to promote sprouting.

mechanisms.name: Arteriovenous identity specification in brain endothelium
mechanisms.summary: A cluster of program genes defines arteriovenous identity and brain-specific arterial EC specialization during postnatal development. Hopx is specifically enriched in intracranial (vs. extracranial) arterial endothelial cells, contributing to their anti-atherosclerotic and immune-quiescent phenotype. Angpt2 marks venous/non-arterial ECs and is actively repressed by arterial-identity transcription factors in brain ECs; conversely its expression defines the venous or angiogenic side of arteriovenous patterning. Cxcr4 is rapidly downregulated upon arterial connection in brain capillaries, delineating the arterial-venous boundary. Rgs6 supports Notch-dependent arterial specification and neurovascularization. Tek (Tie2) counterbalances Angpt2 to modulate arteriovenous tone, consistent with its positive log2fc (program increases when Tek is knocked out).

mechanisms.name: BBB transport homeostasis and endothelial mechanosensing via ion channels
mechanisms.summary: Two program genes, Slc1a1 and Kcnj2, reflect distinct but complementary aspects of brain endothelial cell specialization: BBB metabolite transport and flow-sensitive ion channel function. Slc1a1/EAAT-3 is expressed in brain endothelial cells and mediates polarized brain-to-blood glutamate transport across the BBB, critical for maintaining low interstitial glutamate to prevent excitotoxicity. Kcnj2/Kir2.1 is a flow-sensitive inwardly rectifying K+ channel in endothelial cells, mediating mechanotransduction in response to fluid shear stress; its disruption (e.g., via glycocalyx damage) abolishes flow-induced vasodilation. The perturbation regulators Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 (both with log2fc < 0 on knockout, meaning TGF-β signaling promotes the program) are critical for brain endothelial morphogenesis and BBB integrity, with ALK5/Tgfbr1 directly acting in brain endothelial cells to regulate BBB permeability.

mechanisms.name: Sprouting angiogenesis and tip cell specification in brain vasculature
mechanisms.summary: Angpt2, Cxcr4, and Rgs6 together mark an active sprouting/tip cell state in brain endothelial cells. Angpt2 (angiopoietin-2) is upregulated in brain endothelial cells in proangiogenic states, where its rise accompanies downregulation of its receptor TEK to destabilize quiescent vessels and promote angiogenic sprouting. Cxcr4 (chemokine receptor 4) directs tip cell directional migration during brain capillary network formation and controls arterial-venous connection number. Rgs6, a regulator of G-protein signaling, participates in Notch signaling required for arterial specification and neurovascularization. Regulators NRP1 and TEK anchor the angiopoietin-Notch-chemokine axis: NRP1 activates CDC42 for tip cell filopodia formation, while TEK suppression amplifies the proangiogenic program.

mechanisms.name: Endothelial mechanosensitive flow sensing via inward-rectifier potassium channels
mechanisms.summary: Kcnj2 (Kir2.1) encodes a flow-sensitive inwardly rectifying K+ channel that mediates endothelial mechanotransduction and flow-induced vasodilation. The channel is activated by fluid shear stress through the glycocalyx; its downregulation abolishes flow responses in endothelial cells, and its overexpression rescues impaired flow-induced vasodilation in metabolically compromised arteries. Kcnj2 expression is also regulated by oscillating shear stress in endothelial progenitor cells, where it influences their mesenchymal transdifferentiation. This flow-sensing mechanism is relevant to brain endothelial cells that must respond to hemodynamic forces during postnatal cerebrovascular maturation.

evidence_links.context: Mouse hepatocyte-specific knockout, liver histology and transcriptomics
evidence_links.direction: loss-of-function → liver injury
evidence_links.evidence_span: Hepatocyte-specific KO of lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51) ... oval cell proliferation, fibrosis and inflammation, but without steatosis.
evidence_links.finding: Hepatocyte-specific CYP51 KO causes hepatomegaly, oval cell proliferation, fibrosis and inflammation without steatosis; reduced cholesterol esters provoke cell cycle arrest and senescence; dietary cholesterol rescues fibrosis.
evidence_links.limitation: Knockout model; periportal vs. pericentral zonation not explored

evidence_links.context: Mouse hepatocyte-specific knockout, cholesterol biosynthesis

evidence_links.evidence_span: Development of mice with hepatocyte knockout of lanosterol 14α-demethylase (HCyp51-/-) from cholesterol synthesis is characterized by the progressive onset of liver injury.
evidence_links.finding: Hepatocyte Cyp51 KO causes progressive liver injury with ductular reaction and fibrosis beginning at puberty; depletion of RORC ligands (sterols downstream of CYP51) contributes to transcriptional dysregulation; sex-dependent effects.
evidence_links.limitation: Developmental KO; does not specifically address MASLD or aging context
evidence_links.selection_reason: Second independent hepatocyte-specific Cyp51 KO study confirming Cyp51 role in hepatocyte cholesterol synthesis; links sterol intermediates to nuclear receptor signaling.

evidence_links.context: Cancer cell lines, genome-wide CRISPR screen; not hepatocyte-specific
evidence_links.direction: MSMO1/CYP51A1/SC5D: anti-ferroptotic; DHCR7: pro-ferroptotic; all contribute to sterol intermediates
evidence_links.evidence_span: The pathway components, including MSMO1, CYP51A1, EBP and SC5D, function as potential suppressors of ferroptosis, whereas DHCR7 functions as a pro-ferroptotic gene.
evidence_links.finding: MSMO1, CYP51A1, EBP, and SC5D function as suppressors of ferroptosis by synthesizing 7-DHC, an anti-phospholipid-autoxidation sterol intermediate; DHCR7 is pro-ferroptotic by converting 7-DHC to cholesterol. Genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screen in cancer cells.
evidence_links.limitation: Not hepatocyte-specific; ferroptosis endpoint rather than cholesterol synthesis per se
evidence_links.selection_reason: Genome-wide CRISPR screen identifies MSMO1, CYP51A1, SC5D and DHCR7 as components of the distal cholesterol biosynthesis pathway with distinct roles; covers 4 program genes in one study.

evidence_links.context: Huh-7 HCC cells, mouse liver, AY9944 pharmacological inhibition
evidence_links.direction: DHCR7 promotes cholesterol synthesis at the expense of 7-DHC; inhibition is hepatoprotective
evidence_links.evidence_span: We demonstrate 7-dehydrocholesterol reductase (DHCR7), the terminal enzyme of cholesterol biosynthesis, as a regulator of ferroptosis in hepatocytes.
evidence_links.finding: DHCR7 (7-DHC reductase) is the terminal enzyme of cholesterol biosynthesis in hepatocytes; DHCR7 inhibition increases 7-DHC and suppresses ferroptosis; genetic ablation of Dhcr7 prevents acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure in mice.
evidence_links.limitation: Hepatocellular carcinoma cell line; pharmacological rather than physiological dose range
evidence_links.selection_reason: Directly studies DHCR7 in hepatocytes (Huh-7 cells) and mouse liver; DHCR7 KO prevents acute liver failure, establishing hepatic role.

evidence_links.context: Huh7 hepatoma cells, luciferase assay, chromatin IP, split-luciferase interaction assay

evidence_links.selection_reason: Directly characterizes ERG28 mammalian function; ERG28 KO reduces cholesterol synthesis by 60-75% and interacts with NSDHL and SC4MOL (MSMO1).

evidence_links.selection_reason: Studies FDPS in HepG2 hepatoma cells; FDPS inhibition reduces cholesterol biosynthesis.

mechanisms.name: De novo mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthesis pathway enzymes in hepatocytes
mechanisms.summary: Program P21 encodes nearly the complete enzymatic cascade for de novo sterol biosynthesis via the mevalonate pathway in mouse hepatocytes. Early steps: Hmgcs1 (acetoacetyl-CoA → HMG-CoA), Idi1 (IPP/DMAPP isomerase), Fdps (farnesyl-PP synthase), Mvk/Pmvk/Mvd (mevalonate kinase cascade converting mevalonate to isopentenyl-PP). Squalene synthesis: Fdft1 (squalene synthase, first committed step to sterols). Post-squalene: Lss (lanosterol synthase), Cyp51 (lanosterol 14α-demethylase), Tm7sf2 (sterol C14-reductase), Msmo1/Erg28/Nsdhl (C4-demethylation complex, where ERG28 is the non-catalytic scaffold), Hsd17b7 (zymosterone reductase), Sc5d (lathosterol C5-desaturase), Dhcr7 (7-DHC reductase, last step to cholesterol). Acat2 esterifies the resulting cholesterol. Hepatocyte-specific knockout of Cyp51 causes liver injury (oval cell response, fibrosis); TM7SF2 deficiency causes lipid accumulation and ER stress in regenerating liver. Hepatic expression of NSDHL, HSD17B7, and MSMO1 is well established. The complete pathway is explicitly catalogued in comprehensive reviews of cholesterol biosynthesis.

evidence_links.context: Huh7 hepatoma cells, luciferase assay, ChIP-seq data, KO cell lines
evidence_links.direction: SREBP-2 drives ERG28 transcription; ERG28 loss feeds back to impair SREBP-2 activation
evidence_links.evidence_span: transcription of this gene is driven by the transcription factor SREBP-2 ... KO of ERG28 also impaired the activation of SREBP-2 under sterol-replete conditions.
evidence_links.finding: ERG28 transcription is driven by SREBP-2; ERG28 KO impairs SREBP-2 activation under sterol-replete conditions; ERG28 interacts with NSDHL (SREBP-2 target) and SC4MOL (MSMO1), suggesting ERG28 co-ordinates the C4-demethylation complex under SREBP-2 control.
evidence_links.limitation: Hepatoma cell line; mechanism of SREBP-2 impairment by ERG28 KO is not yet resolved
evidence_links.selection_reason: Directly demonstrates ERG28 is SREBP-2 co-regulated and interacts with other SREBP-2 target enzymes NSDHL and SC4MOL.

evidence_links.context: 107 mouse strains multi-omics discovery, human and mouse hepatocytes, Western diet model
evidence_links.direction: RDH11 is co-regulated with SREBP2 targets; reduced by cholesterol excess, induced by cholesterol depletion
evidence_links.evidence_span: mice fed a Western diet (high fat, high cholesterol) exhibited a significant reduction in hepatic Rdh11 mRNA expression ... RDH11 expression was regulated by altered cellular cholesterol conditions in a manner consistent with SREBP2 target genes HMGCR and LDLR.
evidence_links.finding: Hepatic Rdh11 mRNA is reduced by Western diet (high fat/high cholesterol) and induced ~2-fold by statins in mice; RDH11 expression is regulated by cellular cholesterol status consistent with SREBP2 target genes HMGCR and LDLR; RDH11 modulation in hepatocytes affects cholesterol homeostasis stress response.
evidence_links.limitation: Mechanistic basis for RDH11 in cholesterol homeostasis is not fully established
evidence_links.selection_reason: Directly identifies RDH11 as a novel SREBP2-regulated gene in liver/hepatocytes with a role in cholesterol homeostasis.

evidence_links.context: Mouse NASH models (high-cholesterol diet, MCD diet), primary hepatic stellate cells
evidence_links.direction: High SCAP/low INSIG1 → unrestrained SREBP2 → cholesterol accumulation → NASH fibrosis
evidence_links.evidence_span: HSCs were sensitive to FC accumulation because the high intracellular expression ratio of SREBP cleavage-activating protein (Scap) to insulin-induced gene (Insig) disrupted the SREBP2-mediated feedback regulation of cholesterol homeostasis.
evidence_links.finding: High SCAP:INSIG1 ratio in hepatic stellate cells disrupts SREBP2-mediated feedback regulation of cholesterol; free cholesterol accumulates → TLR4 upregulation → sensitization to TGFβ → fibrosis in NASH mice.
evidence_links.limitation: Hepatic stellate cells, not hepatocytes per se; cholesterol-diet-driven model
evidence_links.selection_reason: Demonstrates SCAP/INSIG imbalance in liver causes disrupted SREBP2 feedback and free cholesterol accumulation in NASH context.

evidence_links.context: Mouse genetic models; review of hepatic and extrahepatic functions
evidence_links.direction: SCAP activates / INSIG1 represses SREBP2-driven cholesterol synthesis
evidence_links.evidence_span: SREBPs are inhibited by a complex composed of INSIG proteins, SREBP cleavage-activating protein (SCAP) and sterols in the endoplasmic reticulum.
evidence_links.finding: Manipulation of SREBP-1, SREBP-2, Scap, Insig-1, Insig-2, and S1P in mice reveals expected lipid metabolism impacts plus diverse physiological roles; establishes SCAP and INSIG1 as central regulators of cholesterol synthesis gene expression in liver.
evidence_links.limitation: Review; individual mechanistic details not re-established
evidence_links.selection_reason: Comprehensive review of mouse Scap, Insig-1, Insig-2, SREBP-1, SREBP-2 knockout and transgenic phenotypes.

evidence_links.context: Mouse hepatocytes, adenoviral delivery, LXR KO mice, HepG2 cells
evidence_links.direction: LDLR enables hepatocyte LDL-cholesterol uptake; regulated by LXR-Idol axis
evidence_links.evidence_span: Idol knockdown in hepatocytes increases LDLR protein levels and promotes LDL uptake.
evidence_links.finding: LXR promotes cholesterol efflux and suppresses LDL uptake by inducing Idol ubiquitin ligase to degrade LDLR; Idol knockdown in hepatocytes increases LDLR protein and LDL uptake; LXR knockout increases LDLR in vivo.
evidence_links.limitation: Focuses on LXR-Idol axis; LDLR function as cholesterol uptake receptor is established background knowledge
evidence_links.selection_reason: Establishes LDLR in hepatocyte cholesterol uptake as complement to de novo synthesis; LXR-Idol axis antagonizes LDLR.

mechanisms.name: SREBP2-mediated transcriptional co-regulation of hepatic cholesterol homeostasis
mechanisms.summary: All mevalonate/cholesterol biosynthesis genes in this program are transcriptionally co-regulated by SREBP-2, whose activation depends on the SCAP-INSIG1 sterol-sensing complex in the ER. When cholesterol is low, SCAP escorts SREBP-2 to the Golgi for proteolytic activation; when sterols are sufficient, INSIG1 retains the complex in the ER. In MASLD/NASH, dysregulated SCAP:INSIG1 ratios in liver cells disrupt feedback and contribute to free cholesterol accumulation. ERG28 (non-catalytic C4-demethylation scaffold) is directly co-regulated by SREBP-2 at the transcriptional level and its loss impairs SREBP-2 activation. RDH11 was identified as a novel SREBP2-regulated gene in hepatocytes, co-regulated with canonical targets HMGCR and LDLR; hepatic RDH11 is reduced by a high-fat/cholesterol diet and induced by statins, implicating it in cholesterol homeostasis stress responses. LDLR, the primary hepatic cholesterol uptake receptor, balances de novo synthesis as a major SREBP-2 target.

evidence_links.context: Mouse liver, stable isotope tracing, hepatocyte-specific ACLY KO, ACSS2 siRNA
evidence_links.direction: ACSS2 provides acetate-derived acetyl-CoA for hepatic lipogenesis when ACLY is bypassed
evidence_links.evidence_span: silencing of hepatic ACSS2, which generates acetyl-CoA from acetate, potently suppresses the conversion of bolus fructose into hepatic acetyl-CoA and fatty acids.
evidence_links.finding: Liver-specific ACLY deletion cannot suppress fructose-induced lipogenesis; gut microbiota convert fructose to acetate, which ACSS2 converts to hepatic acetyl-CoA for lipid synthesis; ACSS2 silencing potently suppresses fructose-driven hepatic lipid accumulation.
evidence_links.limitation: Focuses on fatty acid synthesis; cholesterol synthesis flux not separately quantified
evidence_links.selection_reason: Directly demonstrates hepatic ACSS2 converts microbiota acetate to acetyl-CoA for de novo lipogenesis in liver; ACSS2 silencing suppresses fructose-induced hepatic lipid synthesis.

evidence_links.context: Mouse NAFLD model (high-fat/high-fructose diet), AAV8-shRNA hepatocyte delivery, HepG2 cells
evidence_links.direction: ACSS2 sustains hepatic lipid synthesis in NAFLD when ACLY is blocked; its inhibition improves NAFLD
evidence_links.evidence_span: ACLY inhibition conditionally upregulated DNL enzymes, but consistently activated the ACSS2-acetyl-CoA pathway ... Dual inhibition of ACLY and ACSS2 broke this cycle by reducing hepatic acetyl-CoA flux, suppressing DNL.
evidence_links.finding: ACLY inhibition in NAFLD mice upregulates ACSS2 and activates acetyl-CoA pathway, sustaining lipogenesis; dual ACLY+ACSS2 inhibition breaks this cycle, reducing hepatic lipid accumulation and inflammation while improving mitochondrial function.
evidence_links.limitation: Focuses on fatty acid synthesis; sterol/cholesterol branch not separately measured
evidence_links.selection_reason: Demonstrates ACSS2 drives hepatic lipogenesis in NAFLD context; dual inhibition of ACSS2+ACLY reduces lipid accumulation and inflammation.

evidence_links.context: HepG2 cells, MASLD/MASH in vitro models with palmitic/oleic acid and LPS
evidence_links.direction: DGAT2 promotes triglyceride synthesis in hepatocytes; inhibition reduces MASLD
evidence_links.evidence_span: iDGAT1 and iDGAT2 individually, and even more in combination, reduced TG synthesis in HepG2 cells.
evidence_links.finding: DGAT2 inhibition reduces triglyceride synthesis in HepG2 cells; iDGAT1+iDGAT2 dual inhibition reduces TG content, oxidative stress, and inflammation in hepatocytes under MASLD-like conditions.
evidence_links.limitation: HepG2 cancer cell line; not primary hepatocytes or mouse model
evidence_links.selection_reason: Establishes DGAT2 role in hepatocyte triglyceride synthesis in MASLD; DGAT2 inhibition as therapeutic strategy.

evidence_links.context: Hepatocytes (HepG2), enterocytes (Caco-2), MTP-conditional KO mouse liver, biochemical reconstitution
evidence_links.direction: MTTP promotes hepatic cholesteryl ester synthesis by relieving ACAT2 product inhibition
evidence_links.evidence_span: MTP enhances cellular cholesterol esterification by removing cholesteryl esters from their site of synthesis and depositing them into nascent apoB lipoproteins.
evidence_links.finding: MTP (MTTP) enhances cholesterol esterification by ACAT1/ACAT2 in hepatocytes and enterocytes by removing product (cholesteryl esters) from synthesis site; conditional MTP ablation reduces cholesteryl esters and increases free cholesterol in liver; MTP drives ACAT activity for VLDL packaging.
evidence_links.limitation: Co-studies ACAT1 and ACAT2 without fully separating their individual contributions
evidence_links.selection_reason: Demonstrates MTP (MTTP) enhances ACAT2-mediated cholesteryl ester synthesis in hepatocytes by removing product; links MTTP to cholesterol esterification.

mechanisms.name: Hepatic acetyl-CoA provision and lipid-cholesterol coupling in MASLD context
mechanisms.summary: ACSS2 (acetyl-CoA synthetase short chain 2) converts acetate to acetyl-CoA in hepatocytes, providing the primary carbon substrate for de novo lipogenesis (including cholesterol synthesis) independently of ACLY. When ACLY is inhibited, ACSS2 is upregulated and sustains lipid synthesis, worsening NAFLD; dual ACSS2+ACLY inhibition is required to suppress hepatic lipogenesis. DGAT2 channels diacylglycerol into triglycerides in hepatocytes; DGAT2 inhibition is an established therapeutic target for MASLD, and DGAT2 perturbation (the strongest perturbation regulator for P21) is linked to altered VLDL secretion and cholesterol-driven HCC. MTTP enables VLDL assembly by extracting cholesteryl esters and triglycerides from their synthesis sites; MTP/ACAT2 interaction in hepatocytes shows that MTTP enhances cholesteryl ester synthesis (ACAT2-mediated) by removing product inhibition, coupling sterol esterification to lipoprotein export.

mechanisms.name: De novo hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis via the mevalonate and post-squalene sterol pathway
mechanisms.summary: Nearly all program genes encode sequential enzymes of the two-stage cholesterol biosynthesis pathway. The mevalonate arm (Hmgcs1 → Idi1 → Mvk → Pmvk → Mvd → Fdps → Fdft1) converts acetyl-CoA/mevalonate to farnesyl pyrophosphate and then squalene. The post-squalene arm (Lss → Cyp51 → Msmo1/Nsdhl/Hsd17b7 C4-demethylation complex → Tm7sf2 → Sc5d → Dhcr7) converts lanosterol to cholesterol. Erg28 is a non-catalytic scaffold protein that binds Nsdhl and Msmo1 to facilitate the C4-demethylation complex. Acss2 supplies acetyl-CoA from acetate as the carbon source. Scap and Insig1 directly regulate this entire biosynthetic program through SREBP2 activation in liver.

mechanisms.name: SREBP-2/SCAP/INSIG1 transcriptional control of the hepatic cholesterol synthesis program
mechanisms.summary: The SCAP-SREBP-2-Insig1 axis co-regulates the transcription of nearly all program genes. SCAP escorts SREBP-2 from the ER to Golgi for activation; Insig1 retains SCAP in the ER when sterols are sufficient. Key program genes Erg28 and Dhcr7 carry SREBP-2 binding sites (SREs) in their promoters and are directly transcriptionally regulated. The distinctive gene Rdh11 is co-regulated with canonical SREBP-2 targets (HMGCR, LDLR) in mouse liver and hepatocytes in response to cholesterol status. ERG28 KO itself impairs SREBP-2 activation, revealing a bidirectional relationship between the structural enzyme scaffold and the transcription factor.

mechanisms.name: Hepatic lipid homeostasis and MASLD context: cholesterol esterification, steatosis regulation, and lipid export
mechanisms.summary: In the MASLD disease context of this program, additional distinctive genes and regulators control hepatic lipid balance downstream of cholesterol synthesis. ACAT2 (Acat2) is the dominant cholesterol-esterifying enzyme specifically in hepatocytes, converting excess free cholesterol to cholesterol esters. DDR2 (Ddr2) is markedly downregulated in HFD-fed and genetically obese (MASLD) mouse liver; its overexpression reduces hepatic triglyceride accumulation via the AMPK/ACC pathway. The perturbation regulators Dgat2 (TG synthesis, linked to SREBP-1 cleavage control), Mttp (VLDL assembly and export), and Fads2 (PUFA synthesis modulating de novo lipogenesis) collectively define the hepatic lipid homeostasis network perturbed in MASLD.

mechanisms.name: Bile acid biotransformation: hepatic sulfonation and cysteine-taurine conjugation axis
mechanisms.summary: Distinctive gene Sult2a8 encodes the liver-specific, PPARalpha-regulated sulfotransferase that sulfonates 7alpha-hydroxyl bile acids (the primary bile acid sulfonation pathway in mice), enabling bile acid elimination and cholesterol homeostasis. Program gene Cdo1 encodes the rate-limiting enzyme converting cysteine to cysteinesulfinate, channeling sulfur amino acid catabolism toward taurine, which is the predominant bile acid conjugate in mice. These two complementary pathways — sulfonation (Sult2a8) and taurine conjugation (Cdo1) — together control hepatic bile acid biotransformation and cholesterol handling. Sult2a7 and Sult2a5 are paralogs without retrievable specific papers but likely contribute to the same sulfonation function.

mechanisms.name: Hepatic lipid droplet biogenesis, peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation, and polyol-fructose metabolism
mechanisms.summary: Several program and distinctive genes maintain hepatic lipid homeostasis through three complementary processes. FITM1 (fat storage-inducing transmembrane protein 1) directly binds triglyceride to partition it into lipid droplets at the ER. ECI2 and HAO2 support peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation: ECI2 isomerizes cis-3-enoyl-CoA intermediates during beta-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids, while HAO2 catalyzes peroxisomal 2-hydroxy fatty acid alpha-oxidation. HTATIP2 regulates fatty acid storage and oxidation in hepatocytes. CYB5B participates in the outer mitochondrial membrane amidoxime/lipid reductase system. SORD (sorbitol dehydrogenase) converts sorbitol to fructose in the polyol pathway, linking glucose to fructose metabolism in liver under NRF2 regulation.

mechanisms.name: Bile acid and hydroxysteroid Phase II sulfation and xenobiotic conjugation

Glutathione S-transferase Gsta3 provides the primary Phase II defense against reactive epoxides (e.g. AFB1) in mouse liver. Aldo-keto reductase Akr1c6 participates in prereceptor steroid modulation in the same hepatic niche. Aldh1a1 (RALDH1) handles retinaldehyde and other aldehydes, connecting to NAFLD-relevant vitamin A metabolism. Regulators Insig1 (lipid/sterol sensing) and Abcg5 (biliary sterol export) place this program downstream of hepatic sterol and bile acid homeostasis; Tpst1 co-regulates protein sulfation in the same tissue.

mechanisms.name: Peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplet homeostasis
mechanisms.summary: A cluster of lipid-metabolizing enzymes defines a hepatic peroxisomal/mitochondrial fatty acid metabolism theme. Hao2 (peroxisomal 2-hydroxy acid oxidase) oxidizes 2-hydroxy fatty acids and is downregulated in hepatocarcinogenesis. Aldh3a2 (FALDH) converts long-chain fatty aldehydes from lipid catabolism to fatty acids in liver microsomes. Fitm1 is an ER-resident protein that directly binds triglycerides and partitions them into lipid droplets. Cyb5b on the outer mitochondrial membrane participates in an amidoxime reductase system important for lipid synthesis. Psmd1, a proteasome subunit, modulates hepatocellular lipid droplet accumulation via p38-JNK and AKT-mediated control of lipogenic gene expression. Together these genes represent a hepatocyte program coordinating the oxidation of unusual/unsaturated fatty acids with lipid storage.

mechanisms.name: Hepatic sulfur/nitrogen catabolism, urea cycle support, and metabolic aging signature
mechanisms.summary: Cdo1 (cysteine dioxygenase) converts cysteine to sulfinate/taurine in hepatocytes under bile acid/FXR regulation, controlling the balance between taurine-conjugated bile acids, glutathione, and coenzyme A synthesis. Car5a provides the bicarbonate supply required by carbamoylphosphate synthetase 1 (CPS1) and other anaplerotic enzymes for the urea cycle in hepatocyte mitochondria. Alad (delta-aminolevulinate dehydratase) catalyzes the second step of hepatic heme biosynthesis, regulated by PPARα and metabolic demand. Sord (sorbitol dehydrogenase) converts sorbitol to fructose in the polyol pathway in liver, regulated by NRF2/p62 and linked to glucose flux dysregulation. Rgn/SMP30 (regucalcin) is a calcium-binding protein expressed abundantly in hepatocytes that declines with aging, marking the aging hepatocyte. Perturbation by G6pc and Insr regulators (aging condition) places this program at the intersection of nitrogen, sulfur, and carbohydrate metabolism in aging/MASLD hepatocytes.
